title: Daily routine
goal: Describe your day — getting up, working, eating, sleeping — and use the present tense for habits and things happening now.
intro:
This unit is about verbs. The Pashto present tense is pleasantly simple: one set of endings for every verb, and one form for both 'I do' and 'I am doing'.

The bigger idea in Pashto verbs is **aspect**: almost every verb has an *imperfective* form (an ongoing or repeated action) and a *perfective* form (a single, complete action), and the perfective is usually marked with the stressed prefix **wə́-** (و). In this unit you'll use the imperfective present for routines, and meet the perfective forms you'll need from now on.

grammar.title: The present tense: habits and things happening now
grammar.body:
The Pashto present is formed from the **present stem** + personal endings. The endings are the same for every verb:

زه … **-əm** · ته … **-e** · هغه … **-i**
موږ … **-u** · تاسو … **-əy** · هغوی … **-i**

The present stem often differs from the infinitive, so learn it with each verb: ليکل → **ليک-** (ليکم 'I write'), کتل → **ګور-** (ګورم 'I watch'), تلل → **ځ-** (ځم 'I go'), خوړل → **خور-**.

Compound verbs are made from a noun or adjective + **کول** (transitive: 'make/do') or **کېدل** (intransitive: 'become'): کار کول 'to work', پاکول 'to clean', ويده کېدل 'to fall asleep'.

The same present form covers 'I write' (habit) and 'I'm writing' (now). To stress 'right now', add **اوس** or **همدا اوس**, or use **په … لګيا يم** 'I'm busy …-ing': په ليکلو لګيا يم 'I'm (busy) writing'. It is also used for the near future: سبا ځم 'I'm going tomorrow'.

grammar.title: Aspect: the perfective with و-
grammar.body:
Most Pashto verbs come in two aspects. The **imperfective** (what you've been using) presents an action as ongoing or repeated. The **perfective** presents it as a single complete event, and you need it for the subjunctive ('that I eat'), the future, the past 'did', and many imperatives.

How to make the perfective:
• **Simple verbs** add stressed **wə́-**: خورم → **وخورم** wə́xwrəm, ليکم → **وليکم**, ګورم → **وګورم**. Before a, the و and ا merge: اخلم → **واخلم** wā́xləm.
• **Compounds with کول/کېدل** change the helper: پاکوم → **پاک کړم**, ويده کېږم → **ويده شم**. کول itself → **وکړم**.
• **Verbs with a prefix** move the stress onto the prefix: کېنم kenə́m → **کېنم** kénəm; راځم → **راشم**.
• **Irregular**: ځم → **لاړ شم**.

You will see these perfective forms after بايد and غواړم چې, and in polite requests: وکړئ، وخورئ، کېنئ.

examples.roman: ġwā́ṛəm che kor ta lāṛ shəm.

culture: For many Pashtuns the day is framed by prayer: the dawn prayer gets people up early, and work and visits are arranged around the midday and afternoon prayers. Farmers and shopkeepers start at first light and rest in the heat of the afternoon; in the evening men gather in the حجره or at the bazaar teashop, while women visit one another at home. Friday is a half or full day off in Afghanistan (and a day of special prayers in Pakistan, where Sunday is the weekly holiday).

tip.title: The present: habits and right now
tip.body:
- Present stem + the usual endings: زه **-əm** · ته **-e** · هغه **-i** · موږ **-u** · تاسو **-əy** · هغوی **-i**.
- Learn the stem with the verb: پاڅېدل → پاڅېږ**م**, اغوستل → اغوند**م**.
- One form covers 'I get up' (every day) and 'I'm getting up' (now).

tip.title: Going and coming
tip.body:
- **تلل** 'go' is irregular: ځم · ځې · ځي · ځو · ځئ. **راتلل** 'come': راځم · راځې · راځي …
- The place takes **ته** after it: دفتر **ته** ځم 'I go to the office'.
- 'Work' is کار کول: کار **کوم** 'I work'.

Are you coming to the office tomorrow? (polite)

sentences.roman: muẓ pə moṭár daftár ta dzu.

tip.title: A new stem for the present
tip.body:
- Many verbs change their stem in the present: لوستل → **لول**م 'I read', کتل → **ګور**م 'I watch', اورېدل → **اور**م 'I listen'.
- ليکل is regular: **ليک**م 'I write'.
- Learn the present stem with every new verb — it's the form you'll use most.

sentences.en: My father listens to the news.

sentences.roman: muẓ pə ṣowundzí ke paṣtó lwálu aw líku.
sentences.en: At school we read and write Pashto.

lessons.title: Cooking, cleaning and playing

tip.title: Verbs made with کول and کېدل
tip.body:
- Many verbs are a word + **کول** 'do': کار کول 'work', لوبې کول 'play', پاکول 'clean' (پاک + کول).
- Only the کول part takes the endings: لوبې کو**ي**، پاکو**و**.
- **کېدل** 'become' is the partner for things that happen: ويده کېږم 'I fall asleep', څه کېږي؟ 'what's going on?'

tip.title: One-off actions: the و- form
tip.body:
- For a single, complete action — after **غواړم چې**, **بايد**, and in requests — use the perfective: وهم → **و**وهم, لولم → **و**لولم, ګورو → **و**ګورو.
- Verbs with کول swap it for **کړ-**: پاکوم → پاک **کړم**.
- Habits stay plain: هره ورځ زنګ **وهم** 'I call every day'.
